title: Go SDK: unmarshal adapters and streaming retry patterns for typed structured output
creator: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a robust, ergonomic set of Go helpers for decoding structured outputs from Redwood API responses that works across: single-response JSON, streaming event frames, and error/resume semantics. The goal is a set of unmarshal adapters and generics-based wrappers that make it easy for application code to receive typed structs, handle streaming partials, and retry/resume safely without developers writing boilerplate parsing state machines.

Motivation:
- Existing examples scatter decode helpers and streaming combinators across PRs; consumers still need to stitch together io.Reader, JSON partials, and retry metadata (resume tokens) manually.
- We want a single idiomatic Go surface that:
  1) returns T for non-stream calls, and a typed iterator/chan for streaming calls;
  2) encapsulates retry semantics (idempotency, resume tokens, dedupe of already-consumed chunks);
  3) supports structured output detection (e.g., function call objects, tool responses) and fallback raw tokens.

Design proposal:
1) Generic envelope types
   - type Envelope[T any] struct { Data *T; Raw string; Meta map[string]string } (we will provide a stable, minimal envelope API in the package but keep implementation private)
   - For JSON unmarshalling we offer UnmarshalEnvelope[T](b []byte) (Envelope[T], error) which handles both top-level objects and legacy "choices" wrappers.

2) Streaming ergonomics
   - StreamDecoder[T] abstraction: two ergonomic entrypoints: a) Iterator-style: Next() (T, error) b) Channel-style: Chan() <-chan StreamEvent[T] where StreamEvent contains either a Data (T), a Progress token (string) or a Terminal error.
   - ResumeTokens: the runtime should expose resume tokens in stream frames; our StreamDecoder will expose LastResumeToken() string so callers can checkpoint after stable outputs.

3) Retry/resume patterns
   - Provide a RetryPolicy that includes: MaxAttempts, BackoffPolicy, IdempotencyKeyFunc(ctx) string.
   - For streaming: on transient network failure we will attempt to re-establish a stream by sending the idempotency key + last resume token; the decoder will dedupe frames that overlap with already-emitted stable outputs (tracked by sequence numbers or token offsets embedded in frames).

4) Migration and backwards compatibility
   - Keep UnmarshalEnvelope compatible with existing decode helpers but prefer generics-based surfaces in examples.
   - Provide a small adapter package adapters/legacy that converts older Response decoding patterns into the new Envelope[T] so existing code can incrementally migrate.

5) APIs and examples (sketches)
   - Non-stream example:
     var out MyStruct
     env, err := sdk.UnmarshalEnvelope[MyStruct](respBody)
     if err != nil { return err }
     if env.Data != nil { out = *env.Data } else { // fallback to raw }

   - Streaming example (iterator):
     dec := sdk.NewStreamDecoder[MyStruct](streamReader)
     for {
       item, err := dec.Next()
       if err == io.EOF { break }
       if err != nil { return err }
       // use typed item
     }

   - Streaming example (channel + resume):
     dec := sdk.NewStreamDecoder[MyStruct](streamReader)
     ch := dec.Chan()
     for ev := range ch {
       if ev.Type == "data" { process(ev.Data) }
       if ev.Type == "progress" { checkpoint := dec.LastResumeToken() storeCheckpoint(checkpoint) }
       if ev.Type == "error" { // decide to retry using last checkpoint & idempotency key }
     }

6) Testing and acceptance criteria
   - Unit tests for UnmarshalEnvelope with: pure object, choices wrapper, function call shaped output, and unexpected token sequences.
   - Integration test that simulates a streaming socket that drops mid-stream and verifies the decoder resumes from the correct token and does not duplicate already-emitted messages.
   - Benchmark: decoding throughput for streaming path vs current helpers; target no more than 10% regression on p99 memory compared to current decode helpers.

7) Docs and examples
   - Add a dedicated doc page in SDK README: "Typed structured output and streaming" with the above snippets.
   - Provide migration guide: 3-step path for current codebases to adopt (shim import, switch decoder in request handler, remove legacy parsing).

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Avoid reflection-heavy paths in hot loops; use json.Decoder with UseNumber where appropriate and decode into preallocated buffers where possible.
- Keep the public surface small: prefer constructors NewStreamDecoder[T](r io.Reader, opts...) and helpers UnmarshalEnvelope[T](b []byte).
- Be explicit about concurrency: StreamDecoder.Chan() will spawn a goroutine; callers must drain or Cancel() to avoid leaks.
- We will coordinate with runtime team (ENG-19211) to standardize resume token field names and sequence numbers in stream frames.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- PR with implementation + tests merged to go-sdk main.
- Integration test that proves resume semantics under simulated connection drops (test deterministic).
- Example code published in SDK examples folder and sample app updated.
- Add changelog entry and doc page.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Patel: Initial write-up and proposal posted. Tagged runtime and infra teams for resume semantics alignment. Added ENG-19211 as dependency.

2026-03-02 - Mateo Rossi: Spike completed for iterator vs channel ergonomics. Prefers iterator for simple consumers; will implement both but iterator will be the primary recommendation. Found a tricky edge-case with json.Decoder buffering that affects resume offsets.

2026-03-04 - Priya Menon (reviewer): Suggested adding explicit Cancel() on StreamDecoder to avoid goroutine leaks and clarified that LastResumeToken must be stable only after frame acknowledged by consumer. Also requested clear migration path for legacy "choices" wrappers.

2026-03-07 - Mateo Rossi: Implemented UnmarshalEnvelope[T] and iterator API in feature branch. Added unit tests for choices wrapper and function-call shaped payloads. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412 (DRAFT)
2026-03-09 - Security (Luca Chen): Quick review - no secrets persisted by decoder; confirm resume tokens are treated as non-sensitive by default. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-10 - Mateo Rossi: Updated PR after perf run. Streaming path allocations improved by reusing buffers; integration test for resume semantics added. Requesting reviewer assignment from runtime and SDK leads.
